name: toyota_a25a_fks
source: PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7. 2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS 'Dynamic Force' Atkinson-cycle I4 (2018 Toyota Camry LE), EPA NVFEL Fuel Analysis Report 26781 / Test Data Package (Ann Arbor, MI: US EPA, National Center for Advanced Technology, Version 2020-07, 2020), xlsx '4- 2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS Engine Tier 3 Fuel - Test Data.xlsx'. Cross-referenced against SAE 2019-01-0249 (Kargul et al., 'Benchmarking a 2018 Toyota Camry 2.5-Liter Atkinson Cycle Engine with Cooled-EGR', Table 1: rated power 151 kW @ 6600 rpm, rated torque 249 N*m @ 4800 rpm, geometric CR 13:1). MEASURED wot_torque_nm_vs_rpm: 13 literal points from the 'High Load Final' sheet's Accelerator Pedal == 100.00 rows (chosen over 'High Load Initial' because Initial's Fuel Meter Flow is blank for pedal>50%); (rpm,Nm) rounded to (1dp,2dp) with the xlsx Excel row cited: (1003.1,158.80)[row7] (1153.2,176.65)[row11] (1326.2,172.94)[row13] (1498.7,174.55)[row16] (1728.6,196.62)[row20] (2017.1,216.32)[row23] (2534.9,225.13)[row26] (2995.6,217.81)[row29] (3571.2,228.40)[row32] (4032.2,228.35)[row34] (4493.1,232.04)[row37] (5414.5,229.40)[row42] (5761.0,226.24)[row44]. KNOWN DATA ANOMALY (not corrected, not used): at rpm~1326/1498 the same sheet's pedal==70 rows record HIGHER torque than the pedal==80/100 rows at essentially the same rpm (e.g. 1498 rpm: pedal70=189.62 vs pedal100=174.55 N*m); verified not a column-mapping error; root cause not determined (plausibly a drive-by-wire torque-request non-monotonicity at that speed/mode-transition window); the WOT curve above uses ONLY the literal pedal==100.00 rows, so this anomaly does not enter it. The curve is NOT extended with any published (non-test-cell) point above the highest measured 5761 rpm - Curve1D's own clamped-edge extrapolation covers 5761-6600 rpm (limiter.rpm, see below), holding the last measured value. MEASURED motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm: 10 literal points from the 'Steady State' sheet's Accelerator Pedal == 0 AND Torque < 0 rows (closed-throttle, confirmed zero-fuel via Injector Fuel Flow == 0 at every one of these rows; Fuel Meter Flow shows only sensor noise, -0.002..-0.005 g/s, disregarded): (1326.0,-22.90)[row42] (1498.0,-23.60)[row56] (1728.0,-23.30)[row70] (2017.0,-24.30)[row83] (2535.0,-25.90)[row96] (2996.0,-28.40)[row111] (3571.0,-30.60)[row124] (4032.0,-33.90)[row137] (4493.0,-37.40)[row145] (4954.0,-42.30)[row153]. DERIVED x[0]=0: format requires the curve's first knot at rpm 0; linear extrapolation of the two lowest measured points (1326,-22.90) and (1498,-23.60): slope = (-23.60 - -22.90)/(1498-1326) = -0.0040697674418604815 N*m/rpm; y(0) = -22.90 - slope*1326 = -17.5 N*m (rounded to 2dp). limiter.rpm = 6600, CITED directly from SAE 2019-01-0249 Table 1's rated-power engine speed (151 kW @ 6600 rpm) - a measured/published engine-speed fact, not an extrapolated torque value; the engine's own torque clamp (components.cpp) zeroes output above this speed regardless of curve extent, so citing the real rated-power rpm here is honest even though the WOT curve itself stops at the last measured knot (5761 rpm). ASSUMED (no citable value found in the reviewed report/paper/xlsx 'Test Parameter List' sheet; copied from data/engines/i4_2l_na.json, a plausible-class placeholder, and labeled here as an assumption per PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7 rules): inertia_kgm2, breakaway_torque_nm, idle_rpm, stall_rpm, fire_rpm, start_complete_rpm, dfco_enable_rpm, dfco_reenable_rpm, idle_control, starter, crank_axis_local, initial_state.

fuel_map.source: PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7, out/c7/build_map2.py in the physics_sim worktree (reproducible, not committed - stdlib xlsx parse of the same xlsx as wot_torque_nm_vs_rpm/motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm above). rpm axis = exactly the 10 measured motoring-curve rpm values above (zero interpolation error for m(rpm) at every row). load axis = theta_c, dense near 0 per PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7's instruction. DERIVED for every (rpm,load) node with load>0: target torque T = m(rpm) + load*(w(rpm)-m(rpm)) using this file's own motoring/WOT Curve1D knots (w(4954) has no pedal=100 anchor at that speed line - obtained via Curve1D interpolation of this file's own wot_torque_nm_vs_rpm knots at 4493/5414 rpm, i.e. no data outside this file); fuel flow at that T is then read off a piecewise-linear fit through EVERY measured fired point (Accelerator Pedal > 0, Fuel Meter Flow present) from the Steady State and High Load Final sheets within +-20 rpm of the node's own rpm, sorted by torque; below the lowest such fired point (which occurs for several nodes' load in {0.02,0.05,0.1}, since idle/near-idle theta_c targets a T below any pedal>0 point on record), the flow is a LINEAR (Willans-line) EXTRAPOLATION of the two lowest fired points down to the target T (never clamped to zero for load>0, per PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7's instruction); likewise linear extrapolation of the two highest fired points above the highest recorded T. load==0 column forced to exactly 0.0 (format requirement, docs/data_formats/engine.md). The load-time >100% thermal-efficiency check (docs/data_formats/engine.md's sampled rule: every map node, every cell midpoint/row-mid/col-mid, and every WOT/motoring curve breakpoint crossed with every load node) was run by build_map2.py against this exact table and this file's LHV (41954062 J/kg, data/fuels/tier3_e10_cert.json) and PASSED with margin - maximum observed indicated efficiency 61.92% at rpm=4493, load=0.02, well under 100%; no node required adjustment.
